events.summary: Former Kentucky Gov. Matt Bevin was arrested on September 3 by the Bourbon County Sheriff's Office under a contempt-of-court warrant arising from a divorce and child-support case. The reports say a family-court judge ordered him to provide financial records, found him in contempt after missed deadlines and appearances, and had previously ordered 60 days in jail plus a $500 fine. The arrest and contempt proceeding are reported procedural actions; no criminal conviction is established by these reports, and Bevin remains entitled to applicable due process.
events.reason_for_status: The current-window WUKY report and a separate Louisville Public Media/Kentucky Public Radio report corroborate the arrest, while the National Governors Association independently documents Bevin's Republican affiliation and former state executive role. The underlying warrant citation was not directly accessible through the available interfaces and no direct subject response was located, so this is recorded as an official-action report with medium confidence and auto_publish false rather than as a court finding or conviction.
